title: Why one cheap item can break an ROI model
hook: Would you price ten game assets using the cheapest one?
short_script: Would you price ten game assets using the cheapest one? A previous Farmers World 10-Axe estimate did exactly that, so it understated the capital needed. The model now uses a basket of ten distinct active listings. Its latest estimate is three cents of capital, 0.15% modeled return over 30 days, and 19,649 modeled break-even days. That is an estimate, not a promise—and the current yield is tiny. Visit @GamCryp and tap the first channel profile link to check the assumptions and timestamp.
creative_requirements: Show the ten-item basket concept; do not imply a guaranteed purchase or resale price.
Keep 0.15% labeled as modeled 30-day ROI and 19,649 days labeled as modeled break-even.
Keep the three-cent capital value rounded and show the snapshot timestamp on screen.
